slot.brief: Arrange four species (with varying lone pairs and multiple bonds, e.g. water, ammonia, carbonyl-type, amide-type) in order of decreasing bond angle with justification from VSEPR.

stem: Using VSEPR theory, arrange the indicated bond angles in decreasing order: $\text{CO}_2$ ($\angle\text{OCO}$), $\text{H}_2\text{CO}$ ($\angle\text{OCH}$), $\text{NH}_3$ ($\angle\text{HNH}$) and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($\angle\text{HOH}$).

verdicts.working: CO₂ is linear (180°); H₂CO is trigonal planar with ∠OCH about 122°; NH₃ is about 107°; H₂O is about 104.5°. Thus CO₂ > H₂CO > NH₃ > H₂O.

working:
$\text{CO}_2:180^\circ;\quad \angle\text{OCH in H}_2\text{CO}\approx122^\circ$
$\angle\text{HNH in NH}_3\approx107^\circ;\quad \angle\text{HOH in H}_2\text{O}\approx104.5^\circ$
$180^\circ>122^\circ>107^\circ>104.5^\circ$

Independent check: CO₂ is linear (180°); H₂CO is trigonal planar with ∠OCH about 122°; NH₃ is about 107°; H₂O is about 104.5°. Thus CO₂ > H₂CO > NH₃ > H₂O.
solution:
By VSEPR, $\text{CO}_2$ is linear, while $\text{H}_2\text{CO}$ is trigonal planar; lone-pair repulsion reduces the bond angles in $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
$$180^\\circ > 122^\\text{ (approximately)} > 107^\\text{ (approximately)} > 104.5^\\text{ (approximately)}$$
Thus, $\text{CO}_2 > \text{H}_2\text{CO} > \text{NH}_3 > \text{H}_2\text{O}$.
